raw_response:
I am 52 years old, and I have farmed these fields in Quzhou since I was 17. I only finished primary school, but I know this land better than any book. My family has 22.1 mu. There are six of us, but my sons work in the city, so in the fields it is mostly me and my husband. We hire labor during busy times because 22 mu is too much for two people.

Cotton is my main crop, and I plant 10 mu of it. I use hybrid seeds — the same kind that Old Wang from the next village bought from the seed dealer last year. His cotton looked strong, so I will buy the same bag. For fertilizer, I put 20 kg of nitrogen per mu. I buy urea in 50 kg bags, so that is roughly half a bag per mu. I also spread compound fertilizer for phosphorus and potassium — about 8 kg each per mu. I would rather put a bit more than lose yield. A bad cotton year is a disaster. I irrigate four times from my well: right after planting, at flowering, and twice when the bolls are getting fat. The bollworm always comes here, so I spray seven times. I rotary till before planting. If the weather is normal, I expect about 300 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I have 6 mu of winter wheat that went in last autumn. It is an improved variety. Now at green-up time, I topdress with urea — about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu. I also give it 7 kg phosphorus and 5 kg potassium. I irrigate three times: at greening, at jointing, and at grain filling. Two pesticide sprays. I expect 550 kg per mu.

After I cut the wheat in June, I plant summer maize on those same 6 mu. Hybrid seed, the same kind everyone around here plants. I give it 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. Maize does not need as much water as cotton, but I irrigate twice if the rains do not come. Two pesticide applications. I do not till much, just plant into the wheat stubble to save time. Should get 600 kg per mu.

My stevia is on 6.1 mu. I started this because a buyer came to the village two years ago and said he would purchase the leaves. I plant an improved variety. I give it 12 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. It likes water, so I irrigate four times. Three pesticide sprays. I rotary till that plot. I hope for 800 kg of fresh leaves per mu.

Every decision starts from last year. I look at what I spent and what I got. Fertilizer prices went up, but I cannot cut back — if I lose even 50 kg per mu, that costs me more than the fertilizer I saved. I watch my neighbors. If everyone is putting down a certain amount, I do the same or a little more. With 22 mu, I have to think about the whole budget, but cotton pays the bills, so cotton gets fed first.
